title: Sport weight fingerless mitts
subtitle: Lightweight fingerless mitts in sport-weight wool with afterthought thumb.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts in sport-weight wool, worked in 1x1 rib in the round, with an afterthought thumb. Lighter than DK for spring and autumn wear. Three sizes for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 5th series (1880s), §Light-weight mitts. Fingerless mitts in fine wool at sport and 4-ply weights appear in Weldon's and in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938). Both are out of UK and EU copyright.

knitting.gaugeText: 26 sts x 34 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in 1x1 rib slightly stretched on 3.25 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A yarn weight between 4-ply (fingering) and DK. Works at approximately 24 to 28 stitches per 10 cm on 3 to 3.5 mm needles. Sometimes called 5-ply in older UK patterns.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning to them after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Fingerless mitts in
sport-weight
wool, worked in 1x1 rib in the round, with an
afterthought thumb
, sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

Sport weight gives a lighter fabric than DK with better stitch definition in rib. These are suited to spring and early autumn when a full DK mitt is too warm. The construction is seamless, worked in the round using
magic loop
on a 3.25 mm circular. Budget about 75 g (205 m / 225 yards) of sport-weight wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 75 g (about 205 m / 225 yards) of sport-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.25 mm (UK 10 / US 3) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 2: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for thumb position

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 25 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the thumb

content.text: Gauge
26 stitches and 34 rounds to 10 cm in 1x1 rib slightly stretched on 3.25 mm needles. Sport-weight yarn sits between 4-ply and DK; if you are knitting at 24 stitches per 10 cm, try 3 mm needles.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count and measurement reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 44 (50, 56) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 1x1 rib for 28 (30, 32) rounds. The cuff measures about 8 (9, 9.5) cm.
Hand and thumb position
Work in 1x1 rib for 10 (12, 12) rounds. Place the thumb: knit the first 10 (11, 12) stitches with waste yarn, slip back and knit with main yarn, continue in 1x1 rib to end.
Hand above thumb
Continue in 1x1 rib for 18 (20, 22) more rounds. Bind off in 1x1 rib.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn and pick up 10 (11, 12) stitches above and below the gap. Work 12 (14, 14) rounds of 1x1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Common faults

Fabric pulls in too tightly at the cast-on: sport weight at 3.25 mm needles casts on more tightly than DK. Pull the first row of stitches down slightly after casting on, or use a needle one size up just for the cast-on.
Thumb too snug: the thumb stitches were pulled tight when picked up. Pick up each stitch loosely and spread them before working the first thumb round.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Close any small holes at the thumb corners.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry. Sport weight dries faster than DK.
What to try next
A simple lace column on the back of the hand at sport weight looks more delicate than the same motif in DK. The eyelet-lace fingerless mitts pattern is the natural follow-on at a similar needle size.
